14G.4 A house occupied by one having a plague or contagious disease is to be cleaned and disinfected.

points: This is the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. The leper stays outside the camp; the priest goes forth out of the camp to him and looks whether the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper.
The priest does not heal the plague; he examines the man after the healing and carries out the cleansing the Most High commanded.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: For him that is to be cleansed the priest commands two birds alive and clean, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop. One bird is killed in an earthen vessel over running water.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The living bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet, and the hyssop, is dipped in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water; the priest sprinkles him that is to be cleansed seven times, pronounces him clean, and lets the living bird loose into the open field.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: He that is to be cleansed washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair, and washes himself in water, and comes into the camp; but he tarries abroad out of his tent seven days.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: On the seventh day he shaves all his hair off his head, his beard, and his eyebrows, washes his clothes and his flesh in water, and is clean.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: On the eighth day he brings two he lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, three tenth deals of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering, and one log of oil.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The priest that makes him clean presents him with these things before the Most High at the door of the tabernacle. One he lamb is offered for a trespass offering with the log of oil, waved for a wave offering, and slain in the holy place: as the sin offering is the priest's, so is the trespass offering; it is most holy.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The priest takes of the blood of the trespass offering and puts it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: Of the log of oil the priest pours into his own left hand, sprinkles of it with his finger seven times before the Lord, and puts oil upon the ear, the thumb, and the toe, upon the blood of the trespass offering; the remnant of the oil he pours upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The priest then offers the sin offering to make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed from his uncleanness, kills the burnt offering, and offers the burnt offering and the meat offering upon the altar; the priest makes an atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: If he be poor and cannot get so much, the law makes provision: one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, one tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oil, a log of oil, and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The same order is kept for the poor man: the blood of the trespass offering upon the right ear, the right thumb, and the right great toe, the oil sprinkled seven times and put upon the same places, and the rest of the oil upon his head. This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to get that which pertaineth to his cleansing.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The Most High tells Moses and Aaron that when Israel comes into the land of Canaan, and he puts the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of their possession, the owner shall come and tell the priest, saying, It seemeth to me there is as it were a plague in the house.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The priest commands that the house be emptied before he goes in, that all that is in it be not made unclean; then he looks on the plague, and if it be in the walls with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, in sight lower than the wall, he shuts up the house seven days.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: If at the seventh day the plague be spread in the walls, the stones in which the plague is are taken away and cast into an unclean place without the city; the house is scraped within round about, the dust poured out without the city into an unclean place, and other stones and other mortar are put in their place.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: If the plague come again and break out in the house after the stones were taken away and the house scraped and plastered, the priest looks, and if the plague be spread, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: He breaks down the house, the stones of it, the timber, and all the mortar, and carries them forth out of the city into an unclean place. He that goes into the house while it is shut up is unclean until the even, and he that lies or eats in the house washes his clothes.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: If the priest comes in and looks, and the plague hath not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest pronounces the house clean, because the plague is healed.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The house is cleansed the same way as the leper: two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop; one bird killed in an earthen vessel over running water, the house sprinkled seven times, and the living bird let go out of the city into the open fields; so he makes an atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.

note.label: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing

points: The chapter closes the summary: this is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy and scall, for the leprosy of a garment and of a house, for a rising, a scab, and a bright spot, to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy.
